source.title: Astrocyte-gated multi-timescale plasticity for online continual learning in deep spiking neural networks

confidence_rationale: Provides the counterweight to the Masse/Zenke entries: a slow astrocytic gating variable that integrates activity and dynamically MODULATES whether plasticity is admitted -- suppressing updates in stable regimes and enabling them during distribution shifts -- improves class-incremental continual learning without replay. This is a held, regime-tracking gating STATE (entry/exit governed by the slow variable), which leans toward Q-062 sub-question (2)'s 'held intermediate write-eligible state' adding value beyond instantaneous channel gating + a static importance prior. Tilts toward MECH-368 earning a keep, counterbalancing the other two entries; marked mixed because it is a gating signal layered on eligibility traces, not a literal event-level admission gate, and it is a recent single-group SNN benchmark study.
failure_signatures: The astrocytic variable gates plasticity by regime (stable vs shifting), which is a held, time-integrated state rather than a per-event tag re-read; this is evidence that a held write-eligibility state can ADD value over static consolidation -- against the 'existing combination already suffices' null.

It does not factor its gain against REE's specific stack (mode gating + provenance + consolidation-priority), so it shows a held gating state helps in a generic SNN, not that REE specifically needs MECH-368 on top of MECH-261/094/285.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A slow astrocyte-mediated gating variable that integrates neuronal activity over time dynamically modulates synaptic plasticity -- suppressing weight updates in stable regimes and enabling them during distribution shifts -- and, combined with eligibility traces and a broadcast teaching signal, mitigates catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental continual learning without replay buffers.
mapping.ree_translation: Speaks to Q-062 sub-question (2): is 'write-eligible' a held intermediate STATE with its own entry/exit, or just a salience tag re-read? The astrocytic slow variable is exactly a held, regime-tracking gating state that determines write admission, and it improves continual learning -- evidence that such a state can add value beyond static consolidation-priority, i.e. that MECH-368 might earn a keep rather than being redundant with MECH-261+094+285.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a generic deep-SNN learning rule, not REE's online world-model/policy path, and the astrocytic gate is a continuous plasticity-gain modulator layered on eligibility traces rather than a discrete event-level write-eligible state; it shows a held gating state helps in general, not that REE's existing combination is specifically insufficient.
mapping.source_context: Deep spiking neural networks; neuromorphic benchmarks (N-Caltech101, DVS128 Gesture, Spiking Heidelberg Digits) and class-incremental Split CIFAR-100; online learning, no replay.

confidence_components.notes: Source_quality mid (peer-reviewed Frontiers, but recent single-group SNN benchmark study). Mapping_fidelity moderate: a held regime-gating plasticity state is a good analogue of the MECH-368 'held write-eligible state' question but is a gain modulator, not a discrete admission gate. Transfer_risk substantial: neuromorphic SNN benchmarks -> REE online write path. Included specifically to keep the Q-062 evidence balanced -- it is the entry that leans toward MECH-368 utility.
